items.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I started studying theory with the organist T. Tertius Noble, a very great musician... he asked me to turn pages for him at his weekly organ recitals... All of that cumulatively enriched me and made me move so fast as a studying young musician

ctx.x: But I mean, given the Mendelssohns and the Mozarts, who wrote remarkable music when they were five years old, or certainly, so many composers, by the time they were 10 or 11, they were doing some serious writing.

Well, let me just say that, boy, did I catch up quickly, starting very late, because my progress was phenomenal, if I may say so myself, and was considered so. Because, by the way, as a player, I also developed remarkably quickly. I then picked up the french horn, and by the time I was 16, I was playing professionally. I’m a high-school dropout. I left high school and started playing with the New York Philharmonic and [Arturo] Toscanini. When I started the horn, I was 14, and by 16 I’m playing with the New York…
